wire.headline: GreenMart to Cut 4,800 Jobs in Major Restructuring
sentences: GreenMart has announced the reduction of 4,800 jobs across 120 stores nationwide.
Chief Executive Julian Thorne stated that this restructuring is intended to save 310m GBP.
The company cited a revenue decline of 4.26bn GBP as the primary driver for this decision.
The job cuts are set to take effect from March 2027 and will affect supply chain roles.
Following the announcement, shares dipped 12% in early trading.
Union Unite confirmed that the consultation period begins immediately.
Analysts predict a 12.4p hit to earnings per share resulting from these changes.

PD.headline: Dave Pyle Fears Closure of Manchester Store

sentences.text: GreenMart has announced that it is cutting 4,800 jobs across 120 stores nationwide.

The local council has proposed a 500k GBP grant aimed at retraining.

ND.headline: GreenMart to cut 4,800 jobs in major restructuring

sentences.text: Chief Executive Julian Thorne announced a restructuring plan intended to save 310m GBP for the company.
The company's shares dipped 12% in early trading following the announcement.
Analyst Sarah Vane described the move as overdue for margin recovery.
Local MP Marian Holt demanded a parliamentary inquiry into the planned closures.
Customer group FreshVoice launched a petition against recent price hikes.
GreenMart was founded in 1995 by a brother-in-law duo.
The next phase of the plan targets 200 distribution centre positions.
A regional director cited a 15% footfall drop in Deeside.
Competitor BlueBasket is expanding into the same 40 postcode areas.
A staff morale survey showed that 68% of employees intend to resign.
The legal team is currently reviewing severance packages for 4,800 staff.
Supplier AgroLink warned of contract termination threats.
Online sales grew by 22% despite an overall revenue fall.
